samples.summary: New publication boundary writes model-generated `summary`/`evidence` to a public check run without `redactSecrets`
samples.evidence: `deferredRecord` copies `finding.summary` (line 180) and `finding.evidence` (line 181) straight out of `verdict.json` into `output.text`, and the workflow publishes that verbatim via `github.rest.checks.create` (agent-review-panel.yml:1130-1134) on a PUBLIC repository. `redact.mjs` documents itself as "an unconditional pattern filter at the publication boundary" and exists because a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` was once published through exactly this route — model text interpolated into a lens summary that fanned out to a check-run body (redact.mjs:1-14). Attack chain: PR content prompt-injects a lens (or a security lens legitimately quotes a hardcoded credential it found), the lens emits a `minor`/`nit` finding whose `evidence` contains the credential material, `isDeferred` admits it (non-blocking → deferred), and it is serialised into the advisory check body unfiltered. I could not complete the chain to a live secret: the reviewer subagents are Read/Grep/Glob-only, `persist-credentials: false` keeps the token out of `.git/config` (workflow line 413), and the new step's env carries no secret — so the realistic payload is repo-resident secret material rather than the pipeline's own credentials. Note also this is PARITY with the existing gating channel, which also skips redaction (agent-review-panel.yml:1019, and `summary.md` at review-panel.mjs:3453 is published unredacted at line 1029) — but this change adds a NEW boundary and widens the published population to every minor/nit/backlog finding, so the exposure surface grows.
searchedFor: Grep 'redactSecrets' across the repo (80 hits reviewed) — no call in deferred-findings.mjs and none on the panel's check-run output path
Read scripts/agent/redact.mjs in full (publication-boundary contract, layers 1-5)

samples.summary: `lane`/`noveltyOrigin`/`surfaceScope` are recorded as panel-stamped provenance but are model-forgeable on non-blocking findings
samples.evidence: The docblock at lines 143-162 asserts these fields mean "the panel stamped them", and `renderDeferredSummary` derives its "N demoted" split from `r.lane === "backlog"`. But `annotateFindings` returns non-blocking findings UNTOUCHED (`if (!BLOCKING.has(normalizeSeverity(f.severity))) return f;` — review-panel.mjs:842) and `coerceFindings` passes a well-formed finding through with all its keys (review-panel.mjs:546). A prompt-injected lens can therefore emit `{severity:"minor", lane:"backlog", novelty:{origin:"relocated"}, surface:{scope:"out-of-scope"}}`, and lines 183-185 copy all three into the archive as though the gate had decided them — inflating the "demoted" tally and mislabelling why a finding was not acted on. For blockers the exposure is narrower but non-zero: `annotateFindings` overwrites `lane` (line 847) and `surface` only `if (surface)` / `novelty` only `if (novelty)` (lines 848-853), so a forged `novelty.origin` survives whenever the panel computed none. Gating is unaffected (`routeFinding` reads the computed novelty/surface arguments, not `f.novelty`), so this is record integrity, not an auth bypass. The module could reject any `lane`/`novelty`/`surface` on a finding whose normalised severity is non-blocking, since the gate provably never stamps one there.
searchedFor: Grep 'additionalProperties|coerceFinding|schema:' in review-panel.mjs — LENS_SCHEMA is used for output shaping but extra keys survive coerceFindings

samples.summary: `confidence` is the one model-controlled string copied unclipped, letting one finding evict the whole deferred record
samples.evidence: Every other model-controlled string in `deferredRecord` is bounded — `file` to 300 (line 176), `summary` and `evidence` to 2000 (lines 180-181) — with the stated rationale "so one oversized model string cannot spend the whole budget and push real findings out". Line 179 copies `finding.confidence` with `str()` only, no `clip`. A lens whose output was steered by PR content (or simply a verbose model) can emit a single `minor` finding carrying a 100KB `confidence` value; `buildDeferredText`'s trim then drops records from the tail until the payload fits (lines 258-262), so if the oversized record sits early in manifest order every other lens's deferred findings are discarded and the channel floors at `records: []` with `omitted: total`. The tally keeps that honest, but the archive content is suppressed by attacker-influenceable input. Fix is one `clip(...)` consistent with its neighbours; the test at line 132-137 of the test file asserts the clipping of `summary`/`evidence`/`file` but not `confidence`.
searchedFor: Read deferred-findings.mjs lines 164-186 (deferredRecord) and 240-266 (buildDeferredText trim loop)
Read deferred-findings.test.mjs 'oversized model strings are clipped' test — covers summary/evidence/file only

samples.summary: The check-run creator spreads `name`/`conclusion` from a file without re-asserting the never-gates invariant at the point of use
samples.evidence: The github-script step reads `$RUNNER_TEMP/deferred-findings.json` and passes `check.name` and `check.conclusion` straight to `checks.create` (lines 1130-1134), relying entirely on `assertAdvisory` having run inside the producer. The file is written only by trusted code on a fresh runner, so there is no exploit today — but the invariant that matters (a name outside `agent-review-`, which `set-state.mjs:233` reads by prefix to set `lensBlocked`, and a non-`failure` conclusion) is enforced one process earlier and is not re-checked where the privileged API call happens. A two-line assertion at the call site (`if (!check.name.startsWith('agent-review-') && check.conclusion === 'neutral')`, else `return`) would make the guard hold regardless of what wrote the file, without moving the tested logic out of the module.
searchedFor: Grep for other writers of RUNNER_TEMP in the review-panel job

verdict.reason: Absence claim verified end-to-end. deferred-findings.mjs copies model-generated `finding.summary`/`finding.evidence` with truncation only (lines 180-181, `clip` at 102-105) and imports no redaction module at all (imports at 43-48). Those records are serialised into `output.text` (buildDeferredText:259, buildDeferredCheck:363, written at 420) and published verbatim by the workflow via github.rest.checks.create (agent-review-panel.yml:1107-1111 invoking the module, 1130-1134 publishing `check.output`); grep for `redact` across .github/workflows returns no matches. Upstream is equally unfiltered: writeVerdict (review-panel.mjs:3432-3445) serialises findings raw, severity.mjs has no redact reference, and ask.mjs:842 redacts only the session-log copy of `message.result`, not the structured findings. I enumerated every redactSecrets call site in the repo (hunt*.mjs, hunt-ui*.mjs, metrics.mjs:869, auth-smoke.mjs:99/165/168, session-job-summary.mjs:53, review-round-guard.mjs:54, report-intake.mjs:187-205, guard-verdict.mjs:97/115, review-panel.mjs:1695) and all are on infra-error/detail or hunt-report paths — none on the findings-prose check-run path; gh-checks.mjs has no redact reference. No counterexample exists. In-lane under Security (sensitive data exposure) and blocking at major: redact.mjs:1-46 declares redactSecrets an unconditional filter at the publication boundary precisely because a credential once escaped through this same shape (model text -> lens summary -> check-run body), and layers 3-5 are shape/entropy based so they would fire even though the publishing step holds no credentials in env. Considered and rejected as refutation: .trusted/scripts/agent/deferred-findings.mjs is absent so yml:1094's [ -f ] guard skips the step today — that is a not-yet-live condition, not a secrets guard, and it disappears on merge since .trusted is checked out at ref: main.
